What

What Stump Grinding Actually Involves

Grinding isn't just running a machine over a stump. Here's what a proper Roubic grinding job looks like from start to finish.

Stump grinding is the mechanical pulverization of a tree stump and its surface lateral roots using a rotating carbide-tooth cutter wheel on a self-propelled or tracked grinder. The grinder reduces the stump to wood chips and cuts 6–12 inches below grade — deep enough to remove the visible stump and the surface roots without disturbing the deeper root system. A separate but related service, full-excavation stump removal, uses a mini-excavator to extract the entire root ball when re-planting or hardscape construction requires a clean planting hole.

Why

Why NE Ohio Homeowners Grind Stumps

The most common grinding drivers we see across Cuyahoga and Geauga counties — none of them are theoretical. Every one of these shows up on the estimates Aaron walks each month.

  • Post-removal finishingAn exposed stump is a tripping hazard, a mowing obstacle, and a visually unfinished look left behind after a tree comes down.
  • Pest harborageCarpenter ants, termites, and wood-boring beetles colonize decaying stumps within 2–3 years and migrate to nearby houses, garages, and decks.
  • Re-sprouting speciesMaple, elm, willow, cottonwood, and ailanthus send up vigorous suckers from cut stumps unless the stump is ground out.
  • Landscaping & structuralPreparing for new planting, lawn redesign, or hardscape — and clearing stumps that foul mower blades, foundation drains, and irrigation lines.

What If You Wait

The Cost of Leaving a Stump in the Ground

Every one of these is a concrete consequence we see across Cuyahoga and Geauga counties — not a scare tactic.

Pest Harborage

Decaying stumps draw carpenter ants, termites, and wood-boring beetles within 2–3 years — a colony sets up right next to the house.

Colony Migration to Your Home

Active colonies move from the stump to adjacent houses, garages, and decks. Pest remediation usually costs more than the grinding would have.

Aggressive Re-Sprouting

Maple, elm, willow, cottonwood, and ailanthus send vigorous suckers up from cut stumps that must be cut back or chemically treated again and again.

Mower & Equipment Damage

Buried or partly-buried stumps catch mower blades and complicate every future pass over the area.

Hardscape & Drainage Conflicts

Stumps foul foundation drains and irrigation lines and can heave patios and walkways as the wood decays underneath.

Property-Sale Liability

An exposed stump is a visible liability buyers notice — sellers grind it out to clear the objection before listing.

Common Grinding Questions

Stump Grinding FAQ

Seven answers before you book. Every one from Aaron's actual estimate conversations.

How much does stump grinding cost in NE Ohio?
Stump grinding starts at a $150 per-job minimum. Per-stump pricing typically runs $150–$250 for small stumps under 12", $200–$300 for medium stumps 12–24", $400–$800 for large stumps 24–36", and $500–$1,000 for very large stumps over 36". Cleanup or topsoil backfill adds $50–$150 per job. Multi-stump packages and post-removal package rates lower the per-stump cost.
What's the difference between stump grinding and stump removal?
Stump grinding pulverizes the stump and surface roots in place to 6–12" below grade — fast, less invasive, and it leaves the deeper root system intact. Full-excavation stump removal pulls the entire root ball out with a mini-excavator — it leaves a planting hole or clean foundation pad, but it's more invasive, costs more, and takes longer. Most homeowners want grinding; landscapers and builders sometimes need removal.
How deep do you grind the stump?
Standard grinding is 6–12" below grade. Six inches is enough for re-sodding lawn or planting beds; 12 inches is deeper and supports new tree planting in the same spot. Tell us your plan for the spot and we grind to the right depth.
Do you remove the wood chips?
Customer choice. Three options: leave the chips as mulch on-site (free), haul them off (+$50–$150), or backfill the grinding hole with topsoil and seed (+$100–$150). Most residential customers either leave chips or backfill with topsoil; commercial customers usually want haul-off.
Can I plant a new tree where the stump was ground?
Yes — but plan for it. Standard 6-inch grinding leaves enough root and chip residue that a new tree planted in the exact same spot may struggle. For replanting, ask for 12-inch grinding plus topsoil backfill, and consider planting 2–3 feet from the original trunk position rather than directly over it.
Will grinding damage my lawn or driveway?
Grinding is much less invasive than full-excavation removal. The compact grinder works in a small footprint and leaves only the immediate stump area disturbed. Driveways are protected with plywood mats during equipment movement on premium properties. Some lawn impact is unavoidable in the immediate stump zone, but routine cleanup and topsoil-and-seed restore the area within one growing season.
Do you call 811 before grinding?
Yes — 811 utility mark-out is built into our standard operating procedure on every grinding job, because the grinder cuts below grade near potential buried utilities. It protects your gas, water, and electric lines and protects you from a damaged-utility liability claim. We schedule the locate before the grinder arrives on site.
